overview: The root cause is that `netrc.netrc()` is called unconditionally inside the `else` branch of `Request.open()` (urls.py:1487–1497) with no boolean guard, so `.netrc` credentials silently override any explicitly set `Authorization` header. The fix threads a new `use_netrc` parameter (defaulting to `True` everywhere to preserve backward compatibility) through the entire call stack: `Request.__init__` stores the instance default; `Request.open` accepts a per-call override, resolves it via the existing `_fallback` mechanism, and gates the netrc lookup behind `if use_netrc:`; `open_url` and `fetch_url` accept and forward the parameter; `url_get` and `get_url.main()` wire it from module arguments; `uri()` and `uri.main()` wire it from module arguments; and the `url` lookup plugin exposes it via its DOCUMENTATION options block and forwards it to `open_url`. No existing callers are broken because the default is `True`.

edits.change_rationale: Covers req-001, req-002, req-003, and req-004. req-001: `Request.__init__` has no `use_netrc` parameter and stores no `self.use_netrc` attribute; the netrc lookup fires unconditionally at lines 1487-1497. req-002: `Request.open` lacks `use_netrc` in its signature, lacks the `_fallback` resolution line, and lacks the `if use_netrc:` guard. req-003: `open_url` (lines 1649-1668) lacks `use_netrc` in signature and does not forward it to `Request().open()`. req-004: `fetch_url` (lines 1818-1821, 1898-1905) lacks `use_netrc` in signature and does not forward it to `open_url`.
preserved_findings: The `Request.__init__` method (urls.py:1307-1310) accepts no `use_netrc` parameter.
No `self.use_netrc` attribute is stored anywhere in the `__init__` body (lines 1329-1351).

The netrc lookup in `Request.open()` fires unconditionally in the `else` branch at lines 1487-1497: when no explicit username/password is supplied and `force_basic_auth` is false, `netrc.netrc(os.environ.get('NETRC'))` is always called with no flag to suppress it.

All three required elements are absent: 1. A `use_netrc` keyword argument in `open()`'s signature. 2. A `_fallback` resolution line that merges a per-call value with the stored instance default. 3. A conditional guard (`if use_netrc:`) that prevents the netrc lookup when the caller opts out.
use_proxy follows the same pattern: default in __init__ signature (urls.py:1307), stored as self.use_proxy (urls.py:1332), per-call override via _fallback() in open() (urls.py:1353-1356)

edits.change_rationale: Covers req-009. The `url` lookup plugin's DOCUMENTATION options block (lines 7-167) does not declare a `use_netrc` option, so users cannot configure it. The `run()` method (lines 209-248) does not retrieve `use_netrc` via `self.get_option()` and does not forward it to `open_url()`. Per must_co_edit_relations, adding `use_netrc` forwarding here requires that `open_url` (in urls.py) also accept the parameter — otherwise the forwarded kwarg raises a TypeError. The `use_proxy` pattern (declared in DOCUMENTATION at url.py:25-28, retrieved as `self.get_option('use_proxy')`, forwarded to `open_url`) is the reference for both changes.
